summary: A steel fire tower in Saint Johns County, put out to bid and partly taken down in 2011; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Steel tower with a 7x7 steel cab
facts.status_note: As of the 2011 Record report: partly taken down, with the sections put up for sale; the tower no longer stood whole. No source read gives its current state.

events.note: The Eastern US Lookouts listing says a 100-foot steel tower with a 7x7 steel cab was erected in 1953. The 2011 St. Augustine Record says it was built in 1954 and gives a height of 121 feet.
Bidding on the sale began January 5, 2011; the listing says it sold for $255.00. The Record reports the tower partly dismantled by crane and in four sections, with bids received on the rest.

evidence.supports: 1953 erection, 100-foot steel tower with 7x7 steel cab
evidence.quote: 1953: A 100-foot steel tower with a 7x7 steel cab erected.
January 5, 2011: The beginning date of bidding on the sale of the Durbin Fire Tower. (sold for $255.00)

evidence.supports: tower built 1954 to help detect forest fires
evidence.quote: The steel tower, built in 1954 to help detect forest fires, was made obsolete by radar, cell phones, satellite imagery and airplanes that spot fires much quicker.

evidence.supports: 121-foot height and Florida Division of Forestry ownership
evidence.quote: The Florida Division of Forestry's 121-foot Durbin Tower on U.S. 1 near County Road 210 was partially dismantled Wednesday by a giant crane.
was partially dismantled Wednesday by a giant crane.
the tower is now in four sections.

evidence.supports: bottom 20 feet sold to a Tennessee landowner
evidence.quote: The bottom 20 feet have been sold to a landowner in Tennessee who wants to add it to an 80-foot tower and look out over his land.
Bids have been received on the rest.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The listing gives 1953 and the 2011 Record gives 1954. Not resolved: the event uses the listing year and the story reports both.

The listing gives 100 feet and the 2011 Record gives 121 feet. The metric figures (about 30.5 m and about 37 m) are conversions; neither source prints metric. Not resolved: facts keep the listing figure, which matches the brief, and the story reports both.

sources.title: Dismantling U.S. 1 fire tower (2011 article, Internet Archive copy)

notes_for_editor: Two sources, one of them a newspaper read through the Internet Archive because staugustine.com returned HTTP 403 to the reader; the archived text is the 2011 article. The listing and the Record disagree on build year (1953 vs 1954) and height (100 ft vs 121 ft). Facts keep the listing height to match the brief. No source describes the site today or who holds the sections; access is left unset rather than guessed.
